headline: South Korea's government plans to make individual users, including YouTubers, label deepfakes themselves, widening a duty that now falls only on AI companies.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a ministry draft that would widen a legal duty to ordinary content makers, but its details are undecided.
importance_line: YouTubers and other people who post AI-made video, audio or images in South Korea would be affected first, then AI companies that now carry the whole labelling duty, but this is a draft amendment and the scope of users' duties is still being decided.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports, citing industry officials on 8 Oct, that the Ministry of Science and ICT is drafting an amendment to South Korea's AI Framework Act so that people who make or share deepfakes (AI-made sound, images or video that are hard to tell from real ones) would have to add watermarks themselves, instead of the duty falling only on AI companies. Fines under the current labelling rule are suspended until at least 22 Jan 2027, officials see little room for further delay, and the scope of users' obligations is still under discussion.
notes: English edition is AI-translated from Korean by the paper itself; quotes may not match the original wording. Original reporting credited to Cho Yoon-jin. The article's sentence 'little room to extend the watermarking duty beyond January' is ambiguous (grace period versus duty); the summary says 'little room for further delay'.
